response_json.request: Add a sliding switch on the bottom to provide a convenient on and off function

actions.target: the bottom of the existing model
actions.relational_constraint: The sliding switch must be located on the bottom.
actions.unresolved_reference: The specific face or region constituting the bottom of the model must be identified.
steps: Use part.semantic_orientation to localize the requested bottom: the orientation status is inferred with 0.84 confidence, and view_sides explicitly maps the -Y view to the semantic bottom. The corresponding geometry is section R01, feature F002 Lower housing shell, and B-rep FACE 9 Lower exterior face.

Confirm the localization in the -Y multiview image, where FACE 9 appears as the broad exposed underside of the mouse housing. Do not modify the upper cover F001, scroll-wheel pocket F007, or separate wheel assembly R03.

Select a clear region of FACE 9 away from the housing perimeter, lateral walls F004 and F005, and the projected scroll-wheel pocket at approximately x=24.93 to 30.61 mm and z=43.51 to 59.29 mm. Prefer a centerline or slightly offset underside location with sufficient surrounding material and convenient access when the mouse is inverted.

Create a local datum plane tangent to FACE 9 at the selected switch center. Orient the datum plane with its normal approximately parallel to CAD Y and align the intended slider travel with the housing longitudinal CAD Z direction.

Define named switch parameters before modeling, including aperture length, aperture width, slider travel, recess depth, actuator projection, running clearance, edge fillet radius, and minimum wall thickness. Size these parameters for a compact two-position slide switch while maintaining adequate material around the cutout.
On the tangent datum plane, sketch a centered rounded-rectangle mounting recess. Constrain its long axis parallel to CAD Z and dimension it to accommodate the switch bezel or mounting frame.

Project or reference the usable boundary of FACE 9 into the sketch and verify that the recess remains fully inside the lower-shell face with adequate clearance from its perimeter blends and from the internal scroll-wheel pocket.

Cut the mounting recess inward from FACE 9 in the positive-Y direction. Use a controlled blind depth that creates a shallow seat without unintentionally opening into F007 or breaching the upper housing.

On the floor of the new recess, sketch a narrower rounded slot whose length supports two discrete actuator positions and the required sliding travel. Cut this slot through the local lower-shell thickness to provide clearance for the switch stem or internal contact mechanism.

Create a new switch bezel or mounting frame as either a separate component or an added solid seated in the recess. Model it from a rounded-rectangle sketch, extrude it normal to the local datum plane, and retain a small flange around the actuator slot.
Apply small fillets or chamfers to the exposed bezel edges and to the housing recess entrance. Avoid excessive edge treatment that would reduce the retaining land around the slot.

Create the sliding actuator as a separate solid so it can represent motion independently of SOLID 0. Sketch a capsule-shaped or rounded-rectangle thumb pad over the slot and extrude it outward toward negative Y so that it is accessible but does not project excessively below the desk-contact envelope.

Add a narrower actuator stem beneath the thumb pad and extend it through the slot. Maintain suitable running clearance on both sides and at both ends so the actuator can translate without interference.

Optionally add internal guide rails, stops, or shallow detent geometry beneath FACE 9 to constrain the actuator to one translational degree of freedom along CAD Z and to define stable ON and OFF end positions.

Represent the two functional states by setting the actuator travel endpoints and, if appropriate, adding recessed or engraved ON/OFF, I/O, or 1/0 markings adjacent to the corresponding ends of the slot.

Check that neither actuator endpoint intersects the lower housing, lateral walls, wheel pocket, or wheel assembly. Verify that the cut features preserve the enclosure function of R01 and maintain practical wall thickness around FACE 9.

Validate the final model as a housing solid plus a separate movable switch actuator and, if modeled separately, a bezel or switch body. Confirm that the actuator is visible and operable from the -Y bottom view and that its permitted motion is a two-position slide rather than rotation.
